19. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you. Though the verb is in the past tense, it indicates a present act. It is in order to deal with them with greater urgency that he calls heaven and earth to witness the vengeance of God. In these words he does not address men and angels, as some tamely expound it, but in amplification attributes sense to things inanimate. I pass this over briefly, because I have
See ante on Deuteronomy 4:26, p. 270.
treated it more fully before; as also what soon afterwards follows about life and death. For the Law, as respects its doctrine, contains in it life and death; for the reward of eternal life is not promised in it in vain; but since no one is found worthy of the promised reward, Paul justly teaches that the Law ministers death. Still this is accidental, and proceeds not from any fault in the doctrine, but from the corruption of men. Nevertheless, it is asked how, if the corruption of our nature causes that the Law should engender nothing but death, Moses commands us to “choose life,” which the sinner cannot attain to by it? Thence the Papists uplift their crests, both to extol free-will and to boast of merits; as if Moses did not also testify and proclaim the gratuitous mercy of God, and direct his disciples to Christ in order to seek salvation from Him. When, therefore, he speaks of keeping the Commandments, he does not exclude the two-fold grace of Christ, that believers, being regenerated by the Spirit,
“S’adonnent a observer la Loy, et pource qu’ils n’en peuvent venir a bout, qu’ils ne soyent toujours redevables, que leur fautes leurs soyent gratuitement pardonnees;” should devote themselves to the keeping of the Law; and because they could never attain its end, so as not to be always indebted to it, that their faults should be gratuitously pardoned. — Fr.
should aspire to the obedience of righteousness, and at the same time should be reconciled freely to God through the forgiveness of their sins. And assuredly, since the same covenant is common to us and to the ancient people, it is not to be doubted but that they “chose life” who of old embraced the doctrine of Moses. At the same time, in so far as his legation was different from the Gospel, he rather insists on the office peculiarly entrusted to him, so that the distinction between Christ and himself might more clearly appear. This is the reason why he more sparingly touches upon justification by faith, whilst he enlarges fully on loving and serving God and fulfilling His Commandments.

                  <ns0:p n="1">1 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 26. 40.</ns0:note> AND it shall come to pass, when all these things are come upon thee, the bles<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">When thou art obedient.</ns0:note> and the curse <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">When thou becomest rebelli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous and Apostatical.</ns0:note>, which I have set before thee <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>placed before thy face, i. e.</ns0:hi> propoun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded to thy consideration and choice.</ns0:note>, and thou shalt call them to mind <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>bring</ns0:hi> them <ns0:hi>back to thy heart, i. e.</ns0:hi> deeply affect thy heart with the sence of these things, to wit, of the blessings offered and given to them by Gods mercy, and the curses brought upon themselves by their sins.</ns0:note> among the nations whither the LORD thy God hath driven thee,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And shalt return unto the LORD thy God, and shalt obey his voice, according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children, with all thine heart, and with all thy soul:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 126. 1.</ns0:note> That then the LORD thy God will turn thy captivity <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Bring back thy captives, as <ns0:hi>captivity</ns0:hi> is taken, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 14. 7. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 4. 8.</ns0:note>, and have compassion upon thee, and will return, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 147. 2.</ns0:note> gather thee <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Thy children, either spiritually such, as it is explained <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 11. 51, 52. or literally such, as is promised <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 11.</ns0:note> from all the nations whither the LORD thy God hath scat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tered thee.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Neh. 1. 9.</ns0:note> If <ns0:hi>any</ns0:hi> of thine be driven out unto the<ns0:note place="margin">* Jer. 32. 37.</ns0:note> outmost <ns0:hi>parts</ns0:hi> of heaven, from thence will the LORD thy God gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And the LORD thy God will bring thee into the land which thy fathers possessed, and thou shalt possess it, and he will do thee good, and mul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiply thee above thy fathers.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And * the LORD thy God will circumcise<ns0:note place="margin">Ezek. 11. 19. & 36. 26.</ns0:note> thine heart <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>For the Lord will circum<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>ise thine heart, i. e.</ns0:hi> will by his Word and Spirit change and purge thy heart from all thine Ido<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />latry and Superstition and Wickedness, and encline thy heart to <ns0:hi>love him,</ns0:hi> as it here follows. See <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 10. 16. And so this is pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duced to shew why and how those great things should be ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />complished, God would first convert and sanctifie them, the fruit whereof should be this, that <ns0:hi>they</ns0:hi> should <ns0:hi>return and obey</ns0:hi> Gods <ns0:hi>commandements,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 8. and then should prosper in all things, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9. The Hebrew <ns0:hi>Vau</ns0:hi> is oft rendred <ns0:hi>sor,</ns0:hi> and notes the reason of a thing, as 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 1. 21. and 18. 3, 4 <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 1. 3. and 5. 12. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 16. 2. and 64. 5. And this promise principally respects the times of the Gospel, and the Grace which was to be then imparted to all Gods Israel by Christ, by whom alone this circumcision is obtained, <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 2. 11. And so having fully described to them the Law of God, the Rule of their obedience here<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and in the foregoing chapters, and consi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dering their great instability in the performance of their obedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence to it, he now seasonably adds a glorious Gospel promise, and directs their faith to the Messias by whom alone they could expect or receive the establishment of their hearts in the ways of God against Apostacy.</ns0:note>, and the heart of thy seed, to love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:167" />
with all thy soul, that thou mayest live.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 And the LORD thy God will put all these cur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses upon thine enemies, and on them that hate thee, which persecuted thee.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And thou shalt return, and obey the voice of the LORD, and do all his commandments which I command thee this day.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 28. 11.</ns0:note> And the LORD thy God will make thee plenteous in every work of thine hand, in the fruit of thy body, and in the fruit of thy cattel, and in the fruit of thy land for good <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Whereas thou didst formerly receive and enjoy these mer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cies for thy hurt, through thy own wicked and foolish heart, when thou wast full and fat, forgetting God, and kicking against him, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 31, 20. and 32. 15. now thou shalt have them for thy good, thy heart shall be so changed by the grace of the Gospel that thou shalt not now abuse them, but imploy them to the more chearful and faithful service of God the giver of them.</ns0:note>, for the LORD will again rejoyce over thee for good <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) To do thee good; as he did <ns0:hi>rejoyce to destroy thee,</ns0:hi> Deut. 28. 63.</ns0:note>, as he rejoyced over thy fathers:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 If thou shalt hearken <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">This caution and condition is added to warn them that they should not receive the Grace of God in vain, and to teach them, that the Grace of God doth not discharge mans obligati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on to his duty, nor excuse him for the neglect of it, and that Conversion and Sanctification, though it be Gods work, yet it is mans duty.</ns0:note> unto the voice of the LORD thy God to keep his command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments and his statutes <ns0:hi>which are</ns0:hi> written in this book of the law, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> if thou turn unto the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 For this commandment which I command thee this day <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">He seems to speak of the law, or of that great command of loving and obeying God, mentioned here <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 2, 6, 10, 16. which is the sum of the Law, of which yet he doth not here speak simply, or as it is in it self, but as it is mollified and ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />companied with the Grace of the Gospel, whereby God cir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cumciseth mens hearts to do this, as is expressed, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 6. The meaning is, that although the practise of Gods Law strictly and severely be now far from us, and above our strength, yet, considering the advantage of Gospel Grace, whereby God ena<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bles us in some measure to our duty, and accepts of our sin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cere endeavours in stead of perfection, and imputes Christs per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fect righteousness unto us that believe, now it is near and easie to us. And so this place well agrees with <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 10. 6, &c. where St. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> expounds or applies this place to the righteous<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of faith; by which alone the Law is such as it is here de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scribed.</ns0:note>, it <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 27. 8. Isa. 45. 19.</ns0:note> is not hidden from thee <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>Is not too wonderful for thee,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 17. 8. <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 30. 18. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 32. 17. <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> not too hard for thee to know and do: the Will of God, which is but darkly manifested to other nations, <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 17. 27. is clearly and fully revealed unto thee: thou canst not pretend ignorance or invincible difficulty.</ns0:note>, neither <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> it far off <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Out of thy reach.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 10. 6. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> It <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> not in heaven <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i e</ns0:hi>) Shut up there, but it hath been thence delivered and published by thy hearing.</ns0:note> that thou shouldest say, Who shall go up for us to heaven, and bring it unto us that we may hear it, and do it?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 Neither <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> it beyond the sea <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The knowledge of this commandement is not to be fetch<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed from far distant places, to which divers of the wise Heathens travelled for their wisdome, but it was brought to thy very doors and ears, and declared to thee in this Wilderness.</ns0:note>, that thou shouldest say, Who shall go over the sea for us, and bring it unto us that we may hear it, and do it?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 But the word <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Thou knowest it so well, that it is the matter of thy com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon discourse, thou professest thy knowledge and belief of it: or, in the mouths of thy Priests and Levites, who are dayly preaching of it, and instructing thee in it.</ns0:note>, and in thy heart <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) In thy mind, as the heart is very commonly taken, to understand and believe it.</ns0:note> that thou mayest do it.</ns0:p>

A figure called, Hendiaduo, Or, life, and all the blessings of life, as <ns0:hi>good</ns0:hi> is oft used, as <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 7. 7. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 4. 6. and 128. 5. <ns0:hi>Eccles.</ns0:hi> 2. 24. and 4. 8. and 6. 3.</ns0:note> and death and evil.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 In that I command thee this day, to love the LORD thy God, to walk in his wayes, and to keep his commandments, and his statutes, and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply; and the LORD thy God shall bless thee in the land, whither thou goest to possess it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Either by thy own evil mind, or by the examples or per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swasions of others.</ns0:note>, and worship other gods, and serve them:</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="20">20 That thou mayest love the LORD thy God, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: (for he <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> thy life <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) The cause or author of thy life, as <ns0:hi>life</ns0:hi> is used <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 14: 6. and 17. 3.</ns0:note>, and the length of thy dayes) that thou mayest dwell in the land which the LORD sware unto thy fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob to give them.</ns0:p>
